subject: Intermittent throughput blackout in us-east AZ1 — Exec escalation
messages:
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@brightline.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-10T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Severe throughput drop in us-east AZ1 (prod)

Sean —

We started seeing a pretty sharp drop in throughput this morning around 07:50 PDT for our production traffic routed to us-east AZ1. Throughput is down to ~10% of normal, and 5xx errors have spiked to about 4–6% from baseline <0.1%. Latency (p95) jumped from ~120ms to ~2s.

We attached a trimmed log and a couple of screenshots from our dashboard — errors show underlying model backend timeouts and a stream of "KV cache miss" warnings that correlate with the spike. Can you advise if you can failover Brightline traffic to us-east2 or another region? This is user-impacting for our checkout flows.

Attachments: brightline_error_log_0410.txt; kpi_screenshots_0410.zip

Please escalate; we need ETA and mitigation plan.

— Alex
Alex Wu
Head of SRE, Brightline Health
ops@brightline.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@brightline.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-10T08:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Severe throughput drop in us-east AZ1 (prod)

Alex — thanks for the flag and attachments. I'm escalating immediately to on-call infra and leadership.

Hannah/Monica/Marissa — please triage and provide an initial root-cause hypothesis in 15 minutes. Alex — we may need to steer your traffic to us-east2 while we remediate; Hannah will call out options and impacts. I'll loop in execs if we need capacity or credit decisions.

I know this is high impact — we'll update within 30 minutes.

Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Wu <alex.wu@brightline.com>
Date: 2029-04-10T08:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Severe throughput drop in us-east AZ1 (prod)

Sean / team — initial findings from the runtime and infra telemetry: 

- Timeline: first abnormalities at 07:48 PDT, sustained through current time.
- Symptoms: p50 stable, p95 elevated (120ms -> 2.3s), 5xx rate ~4.8% across customer endpoints, sustained token latency spikes.
- Observed root signals: a burst of KV cache invalidations and misses after a coordinated eviction event in AZ1; this created a cascade of cache warmups that exhausted GPU workers' memory budgets and increased scheduling latency.
- Autoscaler: did not spawn additional Dedicated workers because AZ1 is at physical host capacity for this tenant due to placement constraints; queued requests backlogged in the frontend leading to repeated retries and amplified error-rate.

Suggested immediate mitigations (executive approval may be required for capacity/credits):
1) Emergency cross-region steer of Brightline's prefix to us-east2 (force-evacuation policy) — estimated 5–8 minute propagation, expected to return ~90% of normal throughput but will increase token egress due to longer tails for cold KV cache (~+10% cost during window).
2) Temporary reservation of burst capacity in us-east2 (we can spin ephemeral instances under dedicated pool but need approval to exceed committed capacity) — ETA ~12 minutes to be available.
3) Continue live remediation in AZ1: restart the affected placements and purge the bad eviction pattern; expected stabilization 30–60 minutes but uncertain.

Attachments: p95_kpis_0818.png (screenshots of metrics).

If Sean approves, we'll trigger the forced-evacuation and Monica/Marissa can coordinate comms/credits with Brightline.

— Hannah
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@brightline.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-10T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Severe throughput drop in us-east AZ1 (prod)

Alex — we are so sorry for the disruption. We will prioritize Brightline and coordinate a cross-region steer if the engineering team recommends it. If we proceed with the evacuation, we propose the following customer-facing items:

- Immediate status update acknowledging impact window and mitigation steps (we'll send this within 15 minutes once Eric/Hannah confirm).
- Offer a provisional 10% service credit for the impacted window (subject to final scope) and waive any incident-related overage charges while we remediate.
- Schedule a technical postmortem and a 48-hour exec brief with your ops and our leadership.

Please confirm if you accept the proposed credits and we'd like to know whether Brightline prefers traffic failover now or to wait for AZ1 stabilization.

— Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-10T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Executive escalation: Brightline us-east AZ1 throughput blackout — decision requested (45 min)

Vanessa / Rishi —

Brightline (large customer, production checkout traffic) is experiencing a regional AZ degradation in us-east AZ1 with sustained throughput collapse and elevated 5xx. Ops recommends an emergency cross-region evacuation to us-east2 plus a temporary burst capacity reservation to prevent repeat failures. Customer impact is high (checkout failures), and ops estimates evacuation will restore ~90% throughput within 10 minutes but will incur transient cost and potential for additional token egress (~+10% during recovery).

Requests (need decision within 45 minutes to avoid extended user-impact):
- Approval to force-evacuate Brightline traffic to us-east2 now.
- Authorization to provision ephemeral burst capacity in us-east2 beyond current commitments (estimate: 12 GPUs, 4–6 nodes) to absorb the load for 2–4 hours.
- Authorization to offer a provisional 10% service credit for the impacted window and waive incident overages; authority to finalize with customer.

If approved, ops will proceed immediately and CS will publish a status update and the credit offer. If you need a call, I can get on one in 10 minutes.

Summary metrics attached (ops screenshots).

— Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Alex Wu <alex.wu@brightline.com>
Date: 2029-04-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Executive escalation: Brightline us-east AZ1 throughput blackout — decision requested (45 min)

Approved. Proceed with forced-evacuation to us-east2 and provision the ephemeral burst capacity as requested; prioritize minimizing user impact.

Marissa — please finalize the provisional 10% credit and send the customer comms. Make sure Finance is notified of the temporary capacity authorization and that we track the capacity costs to the BRIGHT-2029-Q2 deal for later reconciliation.

Hannah / Monica — coordinate with our cloud partner for the fastest capacity and confirm when traffic has been fully re-routed. Please post status updates every 10 minutes until stable.

Alex — apologies again for the event. We will get you back to normal traffic and follow up with a full postmortem within 48 hours.

— Vanessa Ortiz
VP, Customer Success Operations, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
